title: Forward product coordinate expansion and compactification transport
statement:
Fix the finite coefficient datum $k,A=A_{E,n}$ of [def-pur-conventions]. Use ordinary unbounded constant-$A$ module derived categories on the small pro-etale sites, with $P_v=Lv^*$, $R_v=Rv_*$, derived tensor $\otimes=\otimes_A^L$ and signed symmetry $\sigma$ [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. Let $f:X\to B$, $g:Z\to B$ be separated finite-type morphisms of separated finite-type $k$-schemes, and choose compactifications $f=aj$, $g=bk$, with opens $j:X\hookrightarrow\bar X$, $k:Z\hookrightarrow\bar Z$ and proper maps $a:\bar X\to B$, $b:\bar Z\to B$ [def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. Put $P=X\times_BZ$, $C=\bar X\times_B\bar Z$, $W=\bar X\times_BZ$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Write $p:P\to X$, $q:P\to Z$, $r:C\to\bar X$, $t:C\to\bar Z$, $v:W\to Z$, $i:W\hookrightarrow C$, $j_q:P\hookrightarrow W$ for the canonical projections and opens; put $u=ij_q$, $h=fp=gq$, $c=bt=ar$. For $M\in D^+(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$, $N\in D^+(Z_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ equipped with etale-origin witnesses [def-weil-pbc-etale-origin-witness], set $H=j_!M$, $J=k_!N$, $D=P_pM\otimes P_qN$, $F=P_rH$, $E=P_iF$, $K=j_{q!}P_pM$, $K_D=j_{q!}D$, $m=i_!K$, $L=R_aH$ and $L_0=P_bL$ [def-weil-extension-by-zero]. Use the specified counit-defined maps $\pi,\operatorname{Ex}_*,\operatorname{Ex}_!,\operatorname{PF}$ of [def-exchange-projection]. All omitted tensor, pullback and direct-image compositors are canonical; the direct-image compositor is $\kappa_{b,t}:R_c\xrightarrow{\sim}R_bR_t$ [lem-weil-derived-direct-image-composition].

Use the unit-normalized open base change $\beta:E\xrightarrow{\sim}K$ and open tensor maps $\delta_{o;Q,V}:o_!Q\otimes V\xrightarrow{\sim}o_!(Q\otimes P_oV)$ of [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization], and the normalized proper/open mate $\Gamma:k_!R_v\to R_ti_!$ of [lem-sf-proper-open-tensor-compatibility]. Write $\epsilon_o:o_!P_o\to1$ for the open-adjunction counit. Set $A_0=\operatorname{Ex}_{*,a,b,H}:L_0\to R_tF$, and let $B_0=\operatorname{Ex}_{!,f,g,M}:P_kL_0\to R_vK$ use the compactification $(j,a)$ and its base change $(j_q,v)$. Put $\chi=\epsilon_{i,F}i_!(\beta^{-1}):m\to F$ and $s=\Gamma_Kk_!(B_0):k_!P_kL_0\to R_tm$.

Require every tensor input and output of the following forward composite to be bounded below with an etale-origin witness. Use the normalized $\alpha$ of [thm-sf-comp-composition] and define
$$T=\alpha_{g,q}\,Rg_!(\operatorname{PF}_{q,P_pM,N})\,Rg_!(\operatorname{Ex}_{!,f,g,M}\otimes1_N)\,Rg_!(\sigma_{N,P_gRf_!M})\,\operatorname{PF}_{g,N,Rf_!M}\,\sigma_{Rf_!M,Rg_!N}:Rf_!M\otimes Rg_!N\to Rh_!D.$$
In the displayed choices for $f,g$, the induced choice $(j_q,v)$ for $q$ and $(u,c)$ for $h$, put
$$d=\delta_{j_q;P_pM,P_vN}:K\otimes P_vN\xrightarrow{\sim}K_D,$$
$$\Psi=\Gamma_{K_D}k_!R_v(d)\,k_!(\pi_{v;K,N})\,k_!(B_0\otimes1_N),\qquad\nu=k_!(\sigma_{N,P_kL_0})\delta_{k;N,L_0}\sigma_{L_0,J},$$
$$z=R_b(\sigma_{J,L_0})\,\pi_{b;J,L}\,\sigma_{L,R_bJ}:L\otimes R_bJ\to R_b(L_0\otimes J).$$
The coordinate expression of the specified forward map is
$$T=\kappa_{b,t}^{-1}R_b(\Psi\nu)z.$$
Its $q$-projection uses exactly the proper factor $\pi_{v;K,N}$ and open factor $d$, and its $g$-projection uses exactly $\pi_{b;J,L}$ and $\delta_{k;N,L_0}$; the symmetry following the latter changes it into $\nu$. No exchange for $q$ is inserted in its projection factor.

Moreover this forward composite commutes with changes of all its chosen compactifications. Precisely, for two systems of choices, let $T_1,T_2$ be the maps and let $\theta_f,\theta_g,\theta_h$ be the normalized common-refinement comparisons of [prop-compactification-coherence-detailed] at $M,N,D$. Then
$$\theta_h(D)T_1=T_2\bigl(\theta_f(M)\otimes\theta_g(N)\bigr).$$
In this equality the exchange and projection factors are transported using their own normalized comparisons, the $q$ comparison being the one for its base-changed compactification; $\alpha$ uses the same normalized endpoint comparisons. Comparisons through further common refinements give the same equality. All compared tensor objects have the stipulated witnesses. The assertion is solely the expansion and change-of-choices compatibility of the forward map; it does not identify it with an ordinary external-product map or assume that a projection or exchange morphism is an isomorphism.

proof.text:
Use the product diagram of the statement. [lem-pur-product-exchange-counit-coordinates] gives that $(j_q,v)$ and $(u,c)$ are compactifications of $q$ and $h$, respectively, and identifies the normalized composition map at every bounded-below witnessed $Q$ on $P$ as
$$\alpha_{g,q,Q}=\kappa_{b,t}^{-1}R_b(\Gamma_{j_{q!}Q}),$$
with $i_!j_{q!}=u_!$ understood. Apply this at $Q=D$. This is allowed by the stipulated witness and lower bound on $D$. In these coordinates $Rf_!M=L$, $Rg_!N=R_bJ$, $P_gL=P_kL_0$, and $Rq_!P_pM=R_vK$.

proof.text:
By [def-exchange-projection], the projection factor for $g=bk$, at inputs $N,L$, is exactly
$$\operatorname{PF}_{g,N,L}=R_b(\delta_{k;N,L_0})\,\pi_{b;J,L}.$$
Here the open projection comparison in that definition equals the unit-normalized $\delta$ by [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization]. It follows that the first three arrows of $T$, including the initial symmetry, form
$$R_b\bigl(k_!(\sigma_{N,P_kL_0})\delta_{k;N,L_0}\bigr)\pi_{b;J,L}\sigma_{L,R_bJ}.$$
The target is $R_bk_!(P_kL_0\otimes N)$.

proof.text:
For the induced compactification $q=vj_q$, [def-exchange-projection] gives
$$\operatorname{PF}_{q,P_pM,N}=R_v(d)\,\pi_{v;K,N},\qquad d=\delta_{j_q;P_pM,P_vN}.$$
The target of $d$ is $j_{q!}(P_pM\otimes P_{j_q}P_vN)=K_D$, since $vj_q=q$. The normalization is again [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization]. The intervening exchange in $T$ is $B_0$ by its definition in the statement. Therefore the next two arrows, after applying $Rg_!=R_bk_!$, are
$$R_bk_!\bigl(R_v(d)\,\pi_{v;K,N}\,(B_0\otimes1_N)\bigr).$$
This expansion has no exchange for $q$: its only two projection factors are the displayed proper projection and open tensor map.

proof.text:
Compose Step 4 with the composition map of Step 1, then with Step 3. Functoriality and associativity give
$$T=\kappa_{b,t}^{-1}R_b\bigl(\Gamma_{K_D}\,k_!R_v(d)\,k_!(\pi_{v;K,N})\,k_!(B_0\otimes1_N)\,\nu\bigr)z
=\kappa_{b,t}^{-1}R_b(\Psi\nu)z.$$
This proves the coordinate formula and both assertions identifying its projection factors.

source.place: Symmetry paragraph: substitution of all forward factors

proof.text:
Write $F_i=Rf_!^{(i)}$, $G_i=Rg_!^{(i)}$, $Q_i=Rq_!^{(i)}$, $H_i=Rh_!^{(i)}$, $A_i=F_iM$ and $X_0=P_pM$. Let $\theta_q:Q_1\cong Q_2$ be the comparison for the induced base-changed compactifications of $q$. The projection/refinement theorem [lem-pur-pf-refinement-compatibility] gives
$$\theta_q(D)\operatorname{PF}_{q,X_0,N}^{(1)}
=\operatorname{PF}_{q,X_0,N}^{(2)}(\theta_q(X_0)\otimes1_N),$$
and
$$\theta_g(N\otimes P_gA_1)\operatorname{PF}_{g,N,A_1}^{(1)}
=\operatorname{PF}_{g,N,A_1}^{(2)}(\theta_g(N)\otimes1_{A_1}).$$
The theorem applies to each refinement and to arbitrary common-refinement comparisons. Its hypotheses are precisely the bounded-below etale-origin conditions on the tensor inputs and outputs required in the statement. Naturality of the projection in its second input also permits replacement of $A_1$ by $A_2$ along $\theta_f(M)$.

source.place: Opening choice-coherence paragraph: separate transport of the two projection factors

proof.text:
On a witnessed bounded-below object $M$, the specified exchanges satisfy
$$\theta_q(X_0)\operatorname{Ex}_{!,f,g,M}^{(1)}
=\operatorname{Ex}_{!,f,g,M}^{(2)}P_g(\theta_f(M)).$$
Indeed [thm-cbc-finite-level-proetale] states independence under the canonical compactification comparisons for the transported finite exchange, on this domain without constructibility or finite Tor hypotheses. Its transported map is the map of [def-exchange-projection]: for the proper factor the counit-mate comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-transport-identifies-exchange] identifies the transported etale mate with this pro-etale mate. For the open factor [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-comparison] identifies the two extensions, and the units in [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization] identify the transported open base change with $\beta$ (both restrict to the identity under the open units). Exactness makes the sheaf comparison degreewise a derived comparison. [lem-sf-class-compact-support-comparison] identifies the composite proper/open functors at the retained witness. That independence uses the etale refinement comparisons transported through the same site comparison $B^c=Rp_*(e_j)\circ\beta_{p,j_!}$. By the first refinement equation of [lem-pur-compact-support-site-coherence], $B^{c'}C(\rho^e_{c',c})=\rho^p_{c',c}C\circ B^c$ on bounded-below etale witnesses, for $f$ and for the base-changed compactifications of $q$; so the transported comparisons are the pro-etale refinement comparisons, and through a common refinement they are exactly $\theta_f(M)$ and $\theta_q(X_0)$ of [prop-compactification-coherence-detailed]. Hence the independence assertion gives exactly the displayed square, with $\theta_q$ for the base-changed compactification. The proper maps in this argument are qcqs, being proper maps of finite-type schemes, as required by the mate-transport lemma.

source.place: Opening choice-coherence paragraph: normalized exchange square on the witnessed domain

proof.text:
The choice-independence and naturality of the normalized composition isomorphism [thm-sf-comp-composition] give at $D$
$$\theta_h(D)\alpha^{(1)}_{g,q,D}
=\alpha^{(2)}_{g,q,D}\,G_2(\theta_q(D))\,\theta_g(Q_1D).$$
This is the composition comparison for the same three endpoint comparisons used above. Its domain is $G_1Q_1D$ and its target is $H_2D$. The theorem preserves the bounded-below witnessed class, so the intervening compact-support images lie in its domain.

source.place: Opening choice-coherence paragraph: normalized composition comparison

proof.text:
To compose these squares explicitly, put
$$\mathcal S_i=G_i(\sigma_{N,P_gA_i})\operatorname{PF}^{(i)}_{g,N,A_i}\sigma_{A_i,G_iN},\qquad e_i=\operatorname{Ex}^{(i)}_{!,f,g,M},\qquad r_i=\operatorname{PF}^{(i)}_{q,X_0,N}.$$
Thus $T_i=\alpha_iG_i(r_i)G_i(e_i\otimes1_N)\mathcal S_i$. Step 6 and naturality of the two symmetries yield
$$G_2(P_g\theta_f(M)\otimes1_N)\theta_g(P_gA_1\otimes N)\mathcal S_1
=\mathcal S_2(\theta_f(M)\otimes\theta_g(N)).$$
Now substitute Step 8 in $\theta_hT_1$ and move $\theta_g$ across $r_1$ and $e_1\otimes1$ by naturality. The result is
$$\alpha_2G_2\bigl(\theta_q(D)r_1(e_1\otimes1_N)\bigr)\theta_g(P_gA_1\otimes N)\mathcal S_1.$$
Steps 6 and 7 replace the expression inside $G_2$ by $r_2(e_2\otimes1_N)(P_g\theta_f(M)\otimes1_N)$. The preceding displayed symmetry/projection equation therefore gives
$$\theta_h(D)T_1=T_2(\theta_f(M)\otimes\theta_g(N)).$$
Only functoriality and the displayed factor squares are used in this multiplication.

source.place: Opening choice-coherence paragraph: multiplication of the separate normalized factor squares

proof.text: Finally, [prop-compactification-coherence-detailed] supplies common refinements for any finite collection of choices and says that the comparisons are independent of that common refinement and satisfy the cocycle condition. Replacing an intermediate common refinement by a further one therefore replaces each $\theta$ by the same morphism, or by a composite equal to it. Applying the equality of Step 9 to successive pairs gives the same equality for the outer pair, since the intermediate comparisons cancel. Thus further common refinements produce exactly the asserted equality. Nothing in Steps 1--9 has inverted a projection or exchange map.

source.place: Opening choice-coherence paragraph: independence of further common refinements
